dedupe.q: on a tower crane when do you call the horizontal part a jib and when do you call it a boom

review.why: Correct under the regulation, though the excerpt omits the (a)(4)(ii) lead-in and the replacement option (B). The correction answers the yes/no question directly.
Both marking the cable and using a spotter are required, and the Category I timing is right. The correction adds that the parts order must be documented.

The phone rule is right, but the signal-guy follow-up should include the §1926.1421 conditions for electronic signals, especially hands-free reception. Those sections aren't in the quoted text but are in Subpart CC.

The anchorage strength and the belt allowance for restraint are right. The extra claim about belts in fall arrest follows §1926.1423(d) literally but clashes with the body-belt ban in the incorporated §1926.502(d), and the question doesn't need it.
All three outcomes are right, but the limits apply to any operator-in-training, so the qualifier 'who isn't certified' wrongly suggests a certified trainee is exempt.

Saying the shift/monthly/annual schedule doesn't apply is too broad. 1441(a) keeps 1412(c) post-assembly inspection and 1413-1414 wire rope rules, and 1413 has its own shift, monthly and annual rope inspections. The correction fixes this.

overrides.note: The independent check's correction named §1926.1421 (voice signals); the device test, dedicated channel and hands-free rules are §1926.1420(a)-(c). Found by the adversarial review.
